message.content:
This looks like a CBP ruling on wood range hood covers. They are non-functional decorative covers that obscure a range hood. Because they are not hoods themselves, parts of range hoods under 8414.90 do not fit. The goods are wooden, so the candidates are 4421 (other articles of wood) or 4418 (builders' joinery and carpentry of wood). Wood hood canopy tops and bases made of wood, MDF, and particle board, and installed on the ceiling, are most likely classified as builders' joinery or carpentry in 4418.79 or 4418.99, or in 4421.99.

Chapter 44 note: 4421 covers other articles of wood. 4418 covers builders' joinery and carpentry, including architectural woodwork. Range hood covers are custom millwork installed in buildings, which makes 4418 plausible. Within 4418, 4418.99 is "other" and splits into 4418.99.10 (edge-glued panels) and 4418.99.90 (other). Another option is 4418.79 (assembled flooring panels), which does not apply. Also considered was 4418.99.9095, but 4418.99.91 is the more specific form: "4418.99.9100 – Other: Other (of wood)". The 4418.99 statistical suffixes are 4418.99.9005 and 4418.99.9095, so I can't be sure of the exact suffix.

The alternative is 4421.99.9880, other wood articles, which fits non-builders' items. I believe the ruling classified them in 4421.99.9880, since they are decorative covers and not joinery that is structural. CBP has treated range hood covers as other articles of wood (4421.99). Since the composition includes MDF and particle board, the heading 4421 residual "other" provision of 4421.99.98 applies, and the statistical suffix 80 applies.
